To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the contribution of Zds family proteins on Cdc55 regulation in budding yeast is greater than that of ENSA family proteins, and the Zds proteins localize in different cellular compartments from ENSA proteins.
Igo1/2 and Cdc55 are localized to the nucleus, and Igo1/ 2 and Zds1/2 inhibit PP2A-CDC55 at different sites and times during mitotic progression.
Igo1 and Igo2 are the budding yeast homologues of ENSA/ENSA2 and that Igo1 is the first example of a PP2A-B55 inhibitor that localizes to the nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the PP2A-CDC55 complex in the cell cycle and how this regulation is conserved in different eukaryotes.
the comparative analysis of the PP2A-CDC55 regulators in yeast and higher eukaryotic cells.
the comparative genetic analysis of PP-2A-Cdc-55 regulators in budding yeasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Zds1/ZDS2 and Igo1/IgO2 play distinct roles in the regulation of PP2A–Cdc55 in budding yeast mitotic progression.
Igo1 and Zds1 have different functions, which are complementary and necessary to regulate Cdc55 during mitotic entry.
the role of ENSA family in Cdc55 inhibition is conserved, whereas the role of ZDS family in Cdc5 inhibition is not conserved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Igo1 is an inhibitor for PP2A-CDC55 and that Zds1 is a nuclear sequestration factor for PP2A- CDC55.
the evolution of Zds1-dependent PP2A-CDC55 sequestration from the nucleus in fungi has facilitated the evolution of closed mitosis in fungi.
Zds1/Zdz2 is the major regulator of PP2A–Cdc55 in yeast mitosis, while Igo1/Igz2 plays a minor role in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of Cdc55 by Zds1/Zd2 is unique to budding yeast, and this mechanism is likely not present in animal cells.
the Zds1/ZDS2 family proteins, which are unique to fungi, are essential for robust mitosis in fungi.
Zds1-family regulators of Cdc55 have a unique function in fungi that is not conserved in higher eukariotes.
